comparator.name: Applied Physics
comparator.sourceNotes: The formally adopted 2026-2027 programme appendix accounts for a complete 180-ECTS Applied Physics bachelor: 60 ECTS in each year. The programme has one Applied Physics major and one deepening Applied Physics minor rather than alternative named routes. Year 3 contains three restricted 5-ECTS choice groups; Atoms & Molecules, Principles of Measurement Systems, and Nanoprobing and Nanofabrication are selected by the neutral official-order tie-break. The public programme page still displays Mathematical Physics in its first-year summary, whereas the current formal appendix lists Differential Equations (for Physics); the formal 2026-2027 appendix governs this reconstruction. The PDF browser metadata retains a legacy '2010-2011' title, but the official TER index and every running header identify the document as the adopted 2026-2027 appendix.

exception.reason: Applied Physics is a cumulative experimental and engineering-physics degree. Its compulsory formation progresses through mechanics and relativity, electromagnetism, quantum and thermal physics, waves and optics, atomic and solid-state physics, fluid physics, materials science, electronics, signal processing, device physics, control engineering, instrumentation and nanofabrication. Four staged laboratory/design components and a 15-ECTS Applied Physics research project integrate that disciplinary sequence. UCR provides useful mathematics, programming, data, robotics and sustainable-energy applications, but no disciplinary physics sequence, experimental-physics laboratories, materials/device/instrumentation formation or physics research capstone. A UCR programme assembled from quantitative and adjacent technology courses would not be a defensible Applied Physics comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-2027 appendix accounts for exactly 180 ECTS: a 60-ECTS mathematics, mechanics, electromagnetism, computation and laboratory first year; a 60-ECTS second year in computation, signal processing, electronics, materials, quantum, atomic, solid-state, thermal, waves/optics, advanced laboratory work and professional context; and a 60-ECTS third year in control, devices, instrumentation, laboratory applications, fluids, solid-state physics, three restricted technical choices and a 15-ECTS research project. The programme defines one Applied Physics major and a deepening Applied Physics minor, with no alternative named route requiring selection.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant mathematical foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming supplies Python and computational problem-solving; DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision and DISDATA312 Robotics apply mathematical methods to imaging, kinematics and motion. ENSENVI111 Dynamic Earth includes broad geophysics, ENSENVI213 Earth System Science Tools uses quantitative modelling, and ENSSUST111 Climate Change and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design address climate and energy applications. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design adds one general design and prototyping experience. The workbook nevertheless contains no course sequence in mechanics and relativity, electromagnetism, quantum physics, thermal or statistical physics, waves and physical optics, atomic or solid-state physics, electronics, fluid physics, materials/device physics, instrumentation, measurement systems, nanofabrication or physical control engineering. It also contains no staged experimental-physics laboratory progression: HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory is biochemical and molecular rather than physical. DISMATH312 studies mathematical linear systems, not laboratory control of physical systems, and DISDATA312 studies robotics rather than engineering-physics instrumentation. No available sequence culminates in an equivalent 15-ECTS Applied Physics research project.
